facts.text: On this date in 1979, Iranian students seized the U.S. Embassy in Tehran, beginning a 444-day hostage crisis that would consume a presidency and reshape Middle East geopolitics.
On this date in 1922, Howard Carter's team uncovered the first step of Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings — the most intact royal burial ever found.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around the city of Mong Khet, Myanmar than outside it — a reminder that Asia's population density defies almost every Western mental map.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in New York or London.
Canada is larger than the entire continent of Europe, yet 90% of its population lives within 160 km of the U.S. border, leaving an area the size of Europe essentially empty.
On Nov 4, 1979, Iranian students seized the U.S. Embassy in Tehran. Oil prices nearly doubled over the next year, triggering the worst U.S. recession since the Great Depression.
On Nov 4, 1922, Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb. Within months, Lloyd's of London was fielding requests to insure against 'the Mummy's Curse' — and declined every one.
The entire U.S. bond market, at roughly $50 trillion, is larger than the U.S. stock market. Most people have never bought a bond.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway collects so much cash from its insurance float that it effectively gets paid to hold investments — the float now exceeds $160 billion.

The Dutch East India Company, often called history's most valuable corporation, was worth an estimated $8 trillion in today's dollars at its 1637 peak — more than all current S&P 500 companies combined.

On this date in 1922, Howard Carter's team uncovered the steps to Tutankhamun's tomb — but the real shock is biological: the pharaoh's DNA revealed he had malaria, a clubfoot, and was likely inbred across multiple generations.
On November 4, 2010, NASA confirmed water ice on the Moon's surface. That ice is ancient — some molecules may have arrived via comets that struck Earth's neighbor before multicellular life existed.
Your skeleton is not static. Osteoclasts dissolve old bone while osteoblasts rebuild it, meaning you replace roughly 10% of your skeleton every year and have an entirely new one within a decade.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors — humans have 3 — yet research shows they process color more efficiently by comparing channels locally, possibly perceiving a richer reality faster than we can imagine.
On this day in 1922, Howard Carter found the first step of Tutankhamun's tomb. The pharaoh had been dead longer by then than the Roman Empire lasted.
On this day in 1979, Iranian students seized the U.S. Embassy in Tehran. The hostage crisis lasted longer than the entire U.S. involvement in World War II.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented his 'electric printing telegraph' in 1843 — Bell's telephone came 33 years later.
Oxford University began teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or never had. It has no direct English translation, which is precisely why it refuses to leave you alone.
Sonder (coined 2012): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. It spread so fast it now appears in formal usage despite being invented yesterday.

On this day in 1922, Howard Carter's team uncovered the first step of Tutankhamun's tomb. The word 'discovery' felt inadequate — Egyptian has 'kashf,' an unveiling, which carries the sense of removing a veil from something already there.
On this day in 1979, Iranian students seized the US Embassy in Tehran. Farsi gave the world 'taarof' — a system of elaborate ritual politeness — a word the hostage crisis rendered grimly ironic.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. It may be the most meaning packed into the fewest speakers of any living language.
On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had burned over 1 million ETH in just three months — permanently removing more supply than many altcoins ever minted.
On this date in 2022, FTX was still processing withdrawals. Binance's public CoinDesk leak response came the following day, triggering the terminal bank run.
Bitcoin's UTXO model means you never actually 'send' coins — you destroy old outputs and create new ones. Your wallet balance is an illusion layered over discrete, unspent receipts.
The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but embedded directly in the coinbase transaction's input script field.

Ethereum validators can be slashed for signing two different blocks at the same height. The penalty scales with how many validators misbehave simultaneously, punishing coordinated attacks most harshly.

On this date in 2016, Microsoft announced it had achieved human parity on a speech recognition benchmark — then quietly noted the test corpus was read speech, not conversation. The caveat outlasted the headline.
On this date in 1952, the UNIVAC predicted Eisenhower's landslide election win within hours of polls closing. CBS aired it reluctantly, suspecting a machine malfunction.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, spent in weeks.
Transformers were introduced in 2017 by eight authors, six of whom left Google within two years. The architecture they published now underlies nearly every frontier model in production.
AlphaFold 2 predicted protein structures for virtually every known protein — around 200 million — in a database released freely in 2022. Structural biology had spent decades solving perhaps 170,000.
